summary: As of August 2026 the FRC swerve problem is solved four times over, and PumpkinLib must not solve it a fifth time. The realistic backends are: (1) CTRE Phoenix 6 26.x `SwerveDrivetrain`/`CommandSwerveDrivetrain` generated by the Tuner X Swerve Project Generator — best-in-class for all-CTRE hardware, gives a native 250 Hz odometry thread, CANivore timesync, `SwerveRequest` control, and `updateSimState()` sim for free; (2) 6328's AdvantageKit swerve templates (`ModuleIO`/`GyroIO`/`PhoenixOdometryThread`/`SparkOdometryThread`) — best for mixed vendors and the only one with deterministic log replay; (3) YAGSL — best JSON-first onboarding and the best driver-input abstraction (`SwerveInputStream`), but the weakest reputation among elite teams and the noisiest Chief Delphi failure-mode traffic; (4) hand-rolled WPILib `SwerveDriveKinematics` + `SwerveDrivePoseEstimator`. WPILib 2026 has quietly changed the hand-rolled contract — `SwerveModuleState.optimize` and `cosineScale` are now **mutating instance methods** and the static `optimize` is deprecated, which silently breaks the classic `state = SwerveModuleState.optimize(...)` idiom. Non-swerve is genuinely neglected: `DifferentialDrive`/`MecanumDrive` still exist in 2026, `RamseteController` is deprecated-for-removal in favor of `LTVUnicycleController`, and WPILib **2027 removes `RamseteCommand`, `SwerveControllerCommand` and `MecanumControllerCommand` outright**, renames `edu.wpi.first` → `org.wpilib`, renames `ChassisSpeeds` → `ChassisVelocities`, makes kinematics immutable, and adds `ChassisAccelerations` — so any PumpkinLib type that leaks WPILib kinematics types into its public API will break in one season. The real, unfilled gaps are: a vendor-neutral drivetrain façade, a single-call bridge wiring PathPlanner + Choreo + vision + AdvantageKit to whichever backend you chose, traction/slip layering via PathPlanner's 254-derived `SwerveSetpointGenerator`, skid detection, a repeatable wheel-radius/feedforward characterization suite with shipped sane defaults per motor, and a teaching-oriented tuner. Those are what PumpkinLib should build; everything else it should adapt.

landscape.tool: CTRE Phoenix 6 Swerve API + Tuner X Swerve Project Generator
landscape.version2026: Phoenix 6 26.1.0 = 2026 Kickoff release; 26.3.0 = current stable javadoc. 26.50.0-alpha-1 = 2027 dev line.
landscape.doesWell: Tuner X generates a complete project: TunerConstants.java + CommandSwerveDrivetrain (implements Subsystem) + Telemetry + a default 'drive straight' auto (new for 2026), and auto-configures PathPlanner AutoBuilder. Dedicated odometry thread synchronous with the motor controllers; with a CANivore + Phoenix Pro timesync all device signals are sampled and timestamped simultaneously for best-possible latency compensation. Full SwerveRequest set in 26.3.0: ApplyFieldSpeeds, ApplyRobotSpeeds, FieldCentric, FieldCentricFacingAngle, RobotCentric, RobotCentricFacingAngle, PointWheelsAt, SwerveDriveBrake, Idle, SysIdSwerveTranslation, SysIdSwerveRotation, SysIdSwerveSteerGains, plus enums ForwardPerspectiveValue and TargetDirectionPerspectiveValue and the NativeSwerveRequest interface. Requests carry withVelocityX/Y, withRotationalRate, withDeadband, withRotationalDeadband, withDriveRequestType, withSteerRequestType, withCenterOfRotation, withDesaturateWheelSpeeds, withForwardPerspective, and withWheelForceFeedforwardsX/Y on the ApplySpeeds variants. SwerveDrivetrain exposes getState() -> SwerveDriveState {Pose, Speeds, ModuleStates, ModuleTargets, ModulePositions, OdometryPeriod, FailedDaqs}, registerTelemetry(Consumer<SwerveDriveState>), setOperatorPerspectiveForward(Rotation2d), seedFieldCentric()/seedFieldCentric(Rotation2d) (new overload for 2026), resetRotation(Rotation2d) (blue-alliance-perspective absolute), resetPose(Pose2d), addVisionMeasurement(...), setControl(SwerveRequest), updateSimState(double dtSeconds, double batteryVolts). New for 2026: LinearPath API (pose-to-pose linear path with velocity/accel limits, TrapezoidProfile-like usage) and WheelForceCalculator (computes wheel force feedforwards from robot mass/MOI). Custom requests are supported by implementing SwerveRequest.apply(...), which runs on the odometry thread.
landscape.gaps: CTRE-hardware-only (all steer controllers must be the same type; drive and steer may differ). Simulation assumes no scrub and no wheel slip and constant drive inertia — CTRE recommends running updateSimState from a 4 ms Notifier rather than the 20 ms loop for realistic PID behavior. Generator does NOT characterize the drivetrain: shipped gains are placeholders. No skid detection, no slip-limited setpoint generation, no wheel-radius characterization. AdvantageKit log replay is not native. 2027 breakage is already visible: ApplyFieldSpeeds/ApplyRobotSpeeds are renamed ApplyFieldVelocity/ApplyRobotVelocity in the 26.50.0-alpha-1 package, and new Device(int id, String canbus) constructors are deprecated and removed in 2027 in favor of new Device(int id, CANBus canbus).
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinDrive.from(TunerConstants.createDrivetrain()) -> CtreSwerveBackend implements PumpkinDrive; driveRobotRelative(speeds, ff) maps to drivetrain.setControl(new SwerveRequest.ApplyRobotSpeeds().withSpeeds(speeds).withWheelForceFeedforwardsX(ff.robotRelativeForcesXNewtons()).withWheelForceFeedforwardsY(ff.robotRelativeForcesYNewtons())); brake() -> SwerveRequest.SwerveDriveBrake; state pulled from drivetrain.getState().

landscape.version2026: YAGSL 2026 exists and is in use (Chief Delphi 'Yagsl2026 Swerve issue' threads), but the published changelog on docs.yagsl.com only reaches 2025.8.0 — UNVERIFIED what the full 2026 feature delta is.
landscape.doesWell: Entirely JSON-driven: deploy/swerve/{swervedrive.json, controllerproperties.json, physicalproperties.json, pidfproperties.json, modules/{frontleft,frontright,backleft,backright}.json}. swervedrive.json = {imu:{type,id,canbus}, invertedIMU, modules:[...]}. Module json = {drive:{type,id,canbus}, angle:{type,id,canbus}, encoder:{type,id,canbus}, inverted:{drive,angle}, absoluteEncoderInverted, absoluteEncoderOffset, location:{front,left}, conversionFactor?}. Motor type strings: sparkmax_neo, sparkmax_neo550, sparkmax_vortex, sparkmax_minion, sparkmax_pulsar, sparkmax_brushed, sparkflex_neo, sparkflex_vortex, sparkflex_minion, sparkflex_pulsar, talonfx, krakenx60, krakenx60foc, falcon500, falcon500foc, talonsrx. Encoders: CANCoder, REV Through Bore, Canandcoder, MA3, SRX Mag, AM Mag, any PWM or analog absolute encoder. IMUs: Pigeon 2, NavX/NavX2, ADIS16448, ADIS16470, any analog gyro (all must be CCW-positive). Ships standard conversion factors for REV MAXSwerve 12/13/14T, SDS MK4 L1-L4, MK4i L1-L3, MK4n L1-L3, MK5i R1-R3, MK5n R1-R3, Thrifty 18T/16T, Plummer corner modules. Best-in-class driver-input DSL: SwerveInputStream with of(SwerveDrive,DoubleSupplier,DoubleSupplier), withControllerRotationAxis, withControllerHeadingAxis, deadband, scaleTranslation, scaleRotation, robotRelative(BooleanSupplier), allianceRelativeControl(BooleanSupplier), headingWhile(BooleanSupplier), cubeRotationControllerAxis, cubeTranslationControllerAxis, translationOnlyWhile, aim(Pose2d)/aimWhile, translationHeadingOffset, driveToPose(Supplier<Pose2d>, ProfiledPIDController, ProfiledPIDController), driveToPoseEnabled, atTargetPose(double), get() -> ChassisSpeeds. Heading correction via SwerveController.headingCalculate using PID from controllerproperties.json. Slew rate limiters, wheel locking, absolute-to-relative encoder fallback, offset offloading (pushOffsetsToEncoders/restoreInternalOffset now deprecated in 2026).
landscape.gaps: YAGSL's own docs tell all-CTRE teams to use Tuner X instead. Odometry documented as continuous 20 ms updates — no high-frequency (100-250 Hz) odometry thread, which is the single largest measurable auto-consistency lever. Chief Delphi carries a persistent stream of YAGSL-specific failures: robot freezing after library update, module angles drifting under aggressive driving, turn motors spinning endlessly at rest, odometry arcing during rotation with AprilTags present. Community consensus is 'great for a team figuring out swerve, wrong for a team that already has PathPlanner + AdvantageKit IO layers + PhotonVision localization.' Closed-loop on-controller PID only on SparkMAX and TalonFX. Abstraction hides the control math, which is exactly what a teaching library should not do at the tuning layer.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinDrive.fromYagsl(new File(Filesystem.getDeployDirectory(),"swerve")) -> YagslBackend implements PumpkinDrive delegating to swervelib.SwerveDrive.drive(ChassisSpeeds)/setModuleStates/getPose/addVisionMeasurement. Do NOT re-expose SwerveInputStream; port its builder shape into PumpkinLib's own backend-agnostic DriveInputStream.

landscape.version2026: 2026 kickoff release. TalonFX(S) template gained ModuleIOTalonFXS (TalonFXS + CANdi PWM encoders) alongside ModuleIOTalonFX (TalonFX + CANcoder), plus documentation for arbitrary/mixed-vendor hardware.
landscape.doesWell: Three templates: talonfx_swerve, spark_swerve, diff_drive. Hardware abstraction is ModuleIO (+ModuleIOTalonFX/ModuleIOTalonFXS/ModuleIOSpark/ModuleIOSim) and GyroIO (+GyroIOPigeon2/GyroIONavX), with @AutoLog IOInputs enabling bit-exact log replay. High-frequency odometry via PhoenixOdometryThread / SparkOdometryThread with a registerSignal(...) hook that explicitly supports mixing vendors on one thread; static final Lock odometryLock (ReentrantLock) guards reads. Drive.java public API: runVelocity(ChassisSpeeds), runCharacterization(double), stop(), stopWithX(), getPose(), getRotation(), setPose(Pose2d), addVisionMeasurement(Pose2d, double, Matrix<N3,N1>), getMaxLinearSpeedMetersPerSec(), getMaxAngularSpeedRadPerSec(), getChassisSpeeds(), getWheelRadiusCharacterizationPositions(), getFFCharacterizationVelocity(), sysIdQuasistatic(Direction), sysIdDynamic(Direction). DriveCommands.java: joystickDrive(Drive, DoubleSupplier x, DoubleSupplier y, DoubleSupplier omega) with 0.1 deadband and squared magnitude; joystickDriveAtAngle(Drive, x, y, Supplier<Rotation2d>) using a ProfiledPIDController at KP=5.0, KD=0.4, maxVel 8.0 rad/s, maxAccel 20.0 rad/s^2 with continuous input -pi..pi; feedforwardCharacterization(Drive) ramping 0.1 V/s after a 2 s orient delay and least-squares-fitting kS and kV; wheelRadiusCharacterization(Drive) spinning in place at 0.05 rad/s^2 to 0.25 rad/s and computing radius = (gyroDelta * DRIVE_BASE_RADIUS) / meanWheelDelta. Uses LocalADStarAK so PathPlanner pathfinding is replay-deterministic. Measured value of high-frequency odometry: 50 Hz mean error 0.388 m / std 0.180 m vs 250 Hz mean 0.297 m / std 0.028 m (23% mean, 84% std improvement); CTRE's own CANivore timesync figures ~15% mean / ~34% std. 2026 additions: unit metadata on all logging interfaces, NT client tracking in SystemStats, LoggedMechanism2d.generate3dMechanism, color logging, online API docs.
landscape.gaps: It is a template you copy and own, not a versioned library — you inherit maintenance and cannot 'upgrade'. No slip/jerk-limited setpoint generation, no skid detection out of the box. Teams that do not use replay pay the IO-layer boilerplate tax for nothing (the common CD verdict: 'AdvantageKit template is only appropriate if you're specifically trying to use log replay'). Spark template defaults ship driveKp=0.0, driveKs=0.0, driveKv=0.1 — deliberately placeholder.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinLib should NOT wrap the template. Instead ship PumpkinLib's ModuleIO/GyroIO-shaped interfaces so an AdvantageKit-template Drive can be adopted with an adapter: PumpkinDrive.fromAdvantageKit(drive) using method references to runVelocity/getPose/addVisionMeasurement/getWheelRadiusCharacterizationPositions. Publish PumpkinLib's own IOInputs as @AutoLog-compatible so replay keeps working.

landscape.doesWell: SwerveDriveKinematics(Translation2d... moduleTranslationsMeters); toSwerveModuleStates(ChassisSpeeds), toSwerveModuleStates(ChassisSpeeds, Translation2d centerOfRotation), toChassisSpeeds(SwerveModuleState...), toTwist2d(SwerveModulePosition...), toTwist2d(SwerveModulePosition[] start, SwerveModulePosition[] end), four desaturateWheelSpeeds overloads (double and unit-typed LinearVelocity/AngularVelocity), resetHeadings(Rotation2d...), copyInto(SwerveModulePosition[], SwerveModulePosition[]). ChassisSpeeds statics: discretize(double,double,double,double), discretize(LinearVelocity,LinearVelocity,AngularVelocity,Time), discretize(ChassisSpeeds,double), fromFieldRelativeSpeeds(...), fromRobotRelativeSpeeds(...); instance toTwist2d(double), plus/minus/times/div/unaryMinus. SwerveDriveOdometry(kinematics, gyroAngle, SwerveModulePosition[], Pose2d), update(Rotation2d, SwerveModulePosition[]), resetPosition(Rotation2d, SwerveModulePosition[], Pose2d). SwerveDrivePoseEstimator(kinematics, gyroAngle, positions, initialPose[, Matrix<N3,N1> stateStdDevs, Matrix<N3,N1> visionStdDevs]); update, updateWithTime(double, Rotation2d, SwerveModulePosition[]), addVisionMeasurement(Pose2d,double) and (Pose2d,double,Matrix<N3,N1>), setVisionMeasurementStdDevs, resetPosition, resetPose, resetTranslation, resetRotation, sampleAt(double). 2026 adds 2D variants of MathUtil.applyDeadband and MathUtil.copySignPow for circular joystick inputs, DCMotor entries for Kraken X44 and Minion, and fixes PoseEstimator resetTranslation/resetRotation teleporting the robot.
landscape.gaps: BREAKING SEMANTIC CHANGE: SwerveModuleState.optimize(Rotation2d) and cosineScale(Rotation2d) are now void mutating INSTANCE methods; the static SwerveModuleState optimize(SwerveModuleState, Rotation2d) is deprecated. Code written as `state = SwerveModuleState.optimize(state, angle)` still compiles against the deprecated static but the idiomatic 2026 form is `state.optimize(currentAngle); state.cosineScale(currentAngle);` — teams that half-migrate silently lose optimization. discretize() is never applied automatically and is the #1 cause of translational drift while rotating. No high-frequency odometry, no threading, no sim.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinDrive.hand(HandRolledSwerveConfig cfg) backend that owns SwerveDriveKinematics + SwerveDrivePoseEstimator and forces discretize + optimize + cosineScale + desaturate in the correct order, so teams cannot get the order wrong.

landscape.doesWell: Ships the 254 setpoint generator as a maintained library rather than copy-paste. new SwerveSetpointGenerator(RobotConfig config, double maxModuleRotationVelocityRadPerSec); generateSetpoint(SwerveSetpoint previousSetpoint, ChassisSpeeds desiredSpeeds, double loopTimeSeconds) -> SwerveSetpoint. SwerveSetpoint(ChassisSpeeds, SwerveModuleState[], DriveFeedforwards) with moduleStates(). Improves on 254's original by limiting module acceleration by max motor torque, capping module torque by wheel-carpet friction to prevent slip, limiting module rotation so centripetal force stays under friction (prevents sliding in curves), and modeling intra-module friction (lower max accel, higher max decel). RobotConfig(double massKG, double MOI, ModuleConfig, Translation2d... moduleOffsets) for holonomic and (massKG, MOI, ModuleConfig, double trackwidthMeters) for differential, plus unit-typed overloads; fields massKG, MOI, moduleConfig, moduleLocations, isHolonomic, numModules, modulePivotDistance, wheelFrictionForce, maxTorqueFriction; static RobotConfig.fromGUISettings() reads the GUI-authored settings file. AutoBuilder.configure(Supplier<Pose2d>, Consumer<Pose2d>, Supplier<ChassisSpeeds>, BiConsumer<ChassisSpeeds,DriveFeedforwards>, PathFollowingController, RobotConfig, BooleanSupplier shouldFlipPath, Subsystem... requirements) for holonomic; the Consumer<ChassisSpeeds> overload for differential. AutoBuilder.shouldFlip(), buildAutoChooser(), followPath(PathPlannerPath), pathfindToPose(Pose2d, PathConstraints).
landscape.gaps: Documented footgun: 'it is important to not discretize speeds before or after using the setpoint generator, as it will discretize them for you' — double-discretization is a silent accuracy bug. Requires accurate mass, MOI, and wheel COF; nobody measures MOI and everyone copies 6.883 from the 6328 template. Not wired to teleop by default — most teams only get slip limiting in auto.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinLib TractionLayer wraps it and inserts it in the ONE funnel (driveRobotRelative), so teleop and auto get identical slip limiting: cfg.traction(TractionMode.SETPOINT_GENERATOR).

landscape.version2026: Choreo 2026, ChoreoLib built against WPILib 2026.1.1-beta-1; .traj schema version 2 adds an `alpha` (chassis angular acceleration, rad/s^2) parameter to DifferentialSample.
landscape.doesWell: Time-optimal trajectory generation with per-module force feedforwards. Java-only AutoFactory higher-level API with trajectoryCmd() and AutoRoutine for branching autos; command-composition style for short autos. Differential support is real (DifferentialSample), which matters for a small-team library.
landscape.gaps: AutoFactory is Java-only. Different mental model and different bind/marker semantics from PathPlanner, so teams pick one and lose the other. No teleop story.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinAuto.configure(drive) should register BOTH AutoBuilder and a Choreo AutoFactory against the same PumpkinDrive, so a team can author in either tool without rewiring: `PumpkinAuto auto = PumpkinAuto.of(drive).withPathPlanner().withChoreo("deploy/choreo");`

landscape.version2026: Tracks WPILib 2026.2.1; includes FRC 2026 REBUILT field and game-piece interactions
landscape.doesWell: dyn4j-based rigid-body swerve simulation with real friction, slip, collisions with field elements and other robots, and game-piece physics — strictly better than CTRE's no-slip sim and better than WPILib flywheel sims for drivetrain feel. Ready-made AdvantageKit-SparkSwerveTemplate-MapleSim and AdvantageKit-TalonSwerveTemplate-MapleSim(-Enhanced) forks; the Enhanced variant simulates the Phoenix motor controllers and CAN bus.
landscape.gaps: Third-party, community-maintained, and delivered as template forks rather than a drop-in — integrating it into an existing project is manual. Requires plausible mass/COF/MOI to be meaningful.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinLib should make maple-sim the default sim backend behind an interface: `DriveSimBackend { MAPLE, CTRE_NATIVE, WPILIB_IDEAL }`, selected by `PumpkinDriveConfig.simBackend(...)`, so the same PumpkinDrive object works in all three.

landscape.version2026: WPILib 2026.x — both classes still present and not deprecated
landscape.doesWell: DifferentialDrive.tankDrive(left,right), arcadeDrive(xSpeed,zRotation), curvatureDrive(xSpeed,zRotation,isQuickTurn). MecanumDrive.driveCartesian(ySpeed,xSpeed,zRotation) and (…, Rotation2d gyroAngle), drivePolar(speed,angle,zRotation). LTVUnicycleController(double dt), (double dt, double maxVelocity), (Vector<N3> qelems, Vector<N2> relems, double dt), (qelems, relems, dt, maxVelocity); calculate(Pose2d current, Pose2d ref, double linearVelRef, double angularVelRef) and calculate(Pose2d, Trajectory.State) both returning ChassisSpeeds; atReference(), setTolerance(Pose2d), setEnabled(boolean). Defaults: tolerances x=0.0625 m, y=0.125 m, heading=2 rad; default max velocity 9 m/s; throws IllegalArgumentException if maxVelocity <=0 or >=15. LTVDifferentialDriveController exists for full state-space diff drive. PathPlanner and Choreo both support differential.
landscape.gaps: RamseteController is deprecated since 2025 and marked for removal — replace with LTVUnicycleController. WPILib 2027 REMOVES RamseteCommand, SwerveControllerCommand and MecanumControllerCommand entirely. Mecanum is effectively unmaintained community-wise. There is no maintained 'good' tank library equivalent to YAGSL/CTRE-swerve; AdvantageKit's diff_drive template (DriveIO + GyroIO, Spark Max / Talon FX / Talon SRX, NavX or Pigeon 2, FF characterization, wheel-radius characterization, velocity PID, sim + replay) is the closest thing and is the model PumpkinLib should follow.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinDrive.differential(DifferentialConfig) implementing the same interface, with driveRobotRelative(ChassisSpeeds) -> DifferentialDriveKinematics.toWheelSpeeds and path following through LTVUnicycleController; getModuleStates() returns an empty array and geometry().isHolonomic() == false so shared layers can degrade gracefully.

landscape.doesWell: new SysIdRoutine(new SysIdRoutine.Config(), new SysIdRoutine.Mechanism(this::voltageDrive, this::logMotors, this)); Config takes quasistatic ramp rate (default 1 V/s), dynamic step voltage (default 7 V), a max test timeout, and a state-change callback. routine.quasistatic(SysIdRoutine.Direction) and routine.dynamic(SysIdRoutine.Direction) return Commands. CTRE provides SysIdSwerveTranslation, SysIdSwerveRotation and SysIdSwerveSteerGains requests so drive translation, drive rotation and steer gains are each characterizable without custom plumbing.
landscape.gaps: Four separate auto routines plus a desktop app plus WPILog wrangling is far too much ceremony for a small team; 6328 explicitly replaced it for kS/kV with an in-code least-squares ramp. SysId does not measure wheel radius, MOI, or COF — the three numbers the setpoint generator actually needs.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinCharacterization should wrap both: `Command kSkV()` (in-code ramp, prints results to console + NT), `Command wheelRadius()`, `Command sysIdFull()` (all four SysId routines chained), `Command slipCurrent()` (wall-push ramp watching stator current/velocity).

landscape.version2026: Changelog shows v2025.1 as the latest tagged version (SPARK MAX firmware 25.0.0, REVLib 2025.0.0). UNVERIFIED whether a 2026 tag exists.
landscape.doesWell: Canonical reference for MAXSwerve geometry and the SPARK config mechanism introduced in REVLib 2025. Notable: the slew rate limiter was REMOVED from the template because it is no longer needed with MAXSwerve 2.0 wheels — a useful data point that slew limiting is a wheel/traction band-aid, not a universal driver-feel feature.
landscape.gaps: Barebones. No pose estimator wiring, no characterization, no high-frequency odometry, no sim. Appears to lag the season.
landscape.integrationShape: Ship the MAXSwerve gear ratios as a PumpkinLib preset (ModulePreset.MAXSWERVE_12T/13T/14T) rather than adapting the template.

landscape.doesWell: This is PumpkinLib's closest existing competitor and worth studying rather than ignoring. IO-centric template covering swerve (250 Hz odometry, momentum-based setpoint calculation, skid detection using FRC 1690's algorithm), mecanum (full holonomic pathfinding + sim), and tank — all three with the same subsystem-level API. Integrates AdvantageKit @AutoLog, PathPlanner + Choreo + on-the-fly pathfinding + drive-to-pose, PhotonVision multi-camera AprilTag fusion with trust-based filtering, Limelight for game-piece detection, dyn4j physics sim, and a SubsystemChecker base class for pit diagnostics. Constants isolated in utils/[branchName]/ so per-mechanism git branches merge cleanly.
landscape.gaps: It is a template/framework you fork, not a versioned dependency; single-team maintenance; not published as a vendordep.
landscape.integrationShape: Not integrable. Treat as the design benchmark: PumpkinLib must at minimum match Consul's tri-drivetrain parity (swerve + mecanum + tank behind one API) and its skid-detection + setpoint-generation layering, but ship as a real versioned library.

capabilities.capability: PumpkinDrive — a single vendor-neutral drivetrain façade with one actuation funnel, adapting CTRE-generated swerve, AdvantageKit-template swerve, YAGSL, hand-rolled swerve, differential and mecanum
capabilities.whyItMatters: A small team's biggest cost is rework: they start on YAGSL because it boots fast, then hit its ceiling and have to rewrite every auto, every vision hook and every drive command to move to CTRE swerve or AdvantageKit. If every PumpkinLib feature (autos, vision fusion, replay, tuning, viz) targets PumpkinDrive instead of a vendor type, changing backends is a one-line change and the team keeps a full season of work. Elite teams get this by writing their own abstraction; a small team can't afford to.
capabilities.prerequisites: Decide early that PumpkinDrive's public types are PumpkinLib-owned records (PumpkinChassisSpeeds/PumpkinPose) OR accept a one-season migration when WPILib 2027 renames ChassisSpeeds to ChassisVelocities, moves edu.wpi.first to org.wpilib, and makes kinematics immutable. Recommend PumpkinLib-owned value types at the boundary with thin converters.

capabilities.capability: PumpkinAuto — one call that wires PathPlanner AutoBuilder, Choreo AutoFactory, alliance flipping and wheel-force feedforwards to whichever backend you chose
capabilities.whyItMatters: This is the exact 'three lines of config' the project stance asks for. AutoBuilder.configure takes 8 arguments and a RobotConfig that most teams get wrong; Choreo needs a separate parallel wiring; shouldFlipPath is a hand-written lambda every team writes slightly differently. Getting this wrong costs a small team an entire competition's autos and is invisible until the red alliance match.
capabilities.prerequisites: PumpkinDrive must expose getRobotRelativeSpeeds and accept DriveFeedforwards, because both PathPlanner and Choreo emit per-module force feedforwards that materially improve path accuracy under acceleration.

capabilities.capability: TractionLayer — slip/jerk-limited setpoint generation inserted into the funnel so TELEOP gets it too
capabilities.whyItMatters: Elite teams run 254's setpoint generator; most mid-tier teams either never adopt it or adopt it only in auto. Because PumpkinDrive has exactly one actuation funnel, PumpkinLib can apply PathPlanner's SwerveSetpointGenerator to driver input as well as trajectories with a single config flag — which is where a small team gets the biggest visible gain (no wheel slip when the driver slams the stick, repeatable auto starts).
capabilities.prerequisites: Accurate massKG, MOI and wheelCOF. Ship a MOI estimator command (spin-up torque vs angular accel) because nobody measures MOI and everyone copies 6.883 from the 6328 template.

capabilities.capability: PumpkinCharacterization — a four-command wizard covering kS/kV, wheel radius, slip current, and MOI, with shipped per-motor defaults
capabilities.whyItMatters: This is where a small team is most obviously behind: they never characterize, so their feedforward is wrong, their odometry scale is wrong (uncharacterized wheel radius, worn tread, carpet compression), their current limits are guesses, and their setpoint generator has garbage inputs. 6328 solved kS/kV and wheel radius in-code without SysId; PumpkinLib should ship that plus the CTRE wall-push slip procedure as one guided routine that writes results to a JSON the team commits.
capabilities.prerequisites: Verified reference values to seed the table. Confirmed data points as of 2026: Tuner X generated TunerConstants ships steer Slot0 kP=100, kI=0, kD=0.5, kS=0.1, kV=1.91, kA=0 and drive Slot0 kP=0.1, kI=0, kD=0, kS=0, kV=0.124, slipCurrent 120 A, speedAt12V 4.69 m/s, coupleRatio 3.818, driveGearRatio 7.3636, steerGearRatio 15.4286, wheelRadius 2.167 in, steerInertia 0.004 kg*m^2, driveInertia 0.025 kg*m^2, steer/drive frictionVoltage 0.2 V. AdvantageKit spark template ships maxSpeed 4.8 m/s, odometryFrequency 100 Hz, trackWidth=wheelBase=26.5 in, wheelRadius 1.5 in, driveMotorReduction (45*22)/(14*15), driveMotorCurrentLimit 50 A, driveKp 0.0, driveKs 0.0, driveKv 0.1, driveSimKv 0.0789, driveSimP 0.05, turnMotorReduction 9424/203, turnMotorCurrentLimit 20 A, turnKp 2.0, turnKd 0.0, robotMassKg 74.088, robotMOI 6.883, wheelCOF 1.2. TalonFX template: ODOMETRY_FREQUENCY 250 Hz on CANivore else 100 Hz. CTRE current-limit guidance for 4 Kraken swerve: 120 A stator / 70 A supply, with wheels observed slipping around 130 A. Community reference for Kraken X60 on WCP Swerve X at 4.59:1 with a 4pi-inch wheel: kV ~0.55, kA ~0.9 (UNVERIFIED as a general default — flag as anecdotal, not shipped).

capabilities.whyItMatters: Skid is the single largest source of odometry divergence, and it is exactly what makes a small team's auto work in the shop and fail on a real field with defense. 1690's algorithm is well known in the elite community and 135's Consul already ships it; nothing publishes it as a library. Detecting skid lets PumpkinLib automatically inflate odometry std-devs, favor vision, and (optionally) back off the setpoint generator — a genuinely elite behavior a small team cannot write themselves.
capabilities.prerequisites: Must be a PumpkinLib original implementation. The 1690 algorithm is described in a public 2024 software session video and reimplemented by others, but there is no canonical open-source Java reference to integrate — BUILD IT and document the math.

capabilities.capability: DriveInputStream — backend-agnostic driver-feel DSL (the good idea in YAGSL, freed from YAGSL)
capabilities.whyItMatters: YAGSL's SwerveInputStream is the single best driver-input API in FRC and it is locked to YAGSL's SwerveDrive. Reimplementing its builder shape over PumpkinDrive means a team on CTRE swerve or AdvantageKit gets alliance-relative control, heading-lock, aim-while, translation-only, cubed axes and drive-to-pose for free — capabilities elite teams hand-roll every year.
capabilities.prerequisites: Note: REV removed the slew rate limiter from the MAXSwerve template because MAXSwerve 2.0 wheels no longer need it. Ship slewRate() OFF by default and document it as a traction band-aid, preferring TractionMode.SETPOINT_GENERATOR.

capabilities.capability: AlliancePerspective — one owner of the blue-origin convention, robot-relative vs field-relative, and the operator perspective
capabilities.whyItMatters: The alliance-flip trap is the classic small-team elimination-match failure: pose origin is always blue, but the DRIVER's forward is alliance-dependent, and resetting heading, flipping paths, and setting operator perspective are three different operations teams routinely conflate. CTRE already separates seedFieldCentric() (driver perspective) from resetRotation(Rotation2d) (absolute blue-perspective) and setOperatorPerspectiveForward(Rotation2d); nothing enforces the distinction across backends.
capabilities.prerequisites: None. This is pure convention enforcement and is the highest value-per-line item in the whole domain.

capabilities.capability: First-class differential/tank and mecanum parity behind PumpkinDrive
capabilities.whyItMatters: The project brief explicitly targets small teams, and small teams run tank. Every competing option (YAGSL, CTRE swerve, AdvantageKit swerve templates) is swerve-only; only 135's unpublished Consul framework achieves tri-drivetrain parity. Shipping differential support that gets the SAME autos, the same vision fusion, the same replay and the same tuner is a genuine differentiator, and it is also the on-ramp: a rookie team starts on tank with PumpkinLib and changes one factory call when they buy swerve.
capabilities.prerequisites: Model on AdvantageKit's diff_drive template (DriveIO + GyroIO, Spark Max / Talon FX / Talon SRX, NavX or Pigeon 2, in-code kS/kV characterization, wheel-radius characterization, velocity PID, sim + replay). Do NOT build on RamseteCommand/SwerveControllerCommand/MecanumControllerCommand — all three are removed in WPILib 2027.

capabilities.capability: PumpkinTuner — live, teaching-oriented PID/FF tuning for drive velocity, steer position and heading lock
capabilities.whyItMatters: The user explicitly asked for tuning software that teaches. Every existing option hides the loop (YAGSL) or dumps raw numbers on you (Tuner X, SysId). A tuner that shows setpoint vs measurement in real time, explains what each term did to the trace, gates you through a fixed order (kS -> kV -> kA -> kP -> kD), and refuses to let a student add kI to a velocity loop is something no FRC tool currently does.
capabilities.prerequisites: Requires the value-logging layer and mechanism visualization to already exist. Depends on AdvantageKit 2026 unit metadata for unit-aware graphing in AdvantageScope. Reuse Tuner X's Multi-device Control & Plot and Integrated Log Analysis (Beta, new for 2026) for CTRE-only teams rather than duplicating them.

capabilities.capability: Unified high-frequency odometry + sim backend selection
capabilities.whyItMatters: Measured: 50 Hz odometry gives mean error 0.388 m / std 0.180 m; 250 Hz gives mean 0.297 m / std 0.028 m — an 84% reduction in variance. That is the difference between an auto that works once and an auto that works every match, and it is invisible to a team that does not know to ask for it. PumpkinLib should make it the default, not an advanced option. Similarly, defaulting sim to maple-sim rather than CTRE's no-slip model means a small team's shop-tested auto behaves like the real field.
capabilities.prerequisites: NATIVE_250HZ requires a CANivore and Phoenix Pro for timesync; degrade to THREADED_100HZ automatically and log a warning rather than silently underperforming. maple-sim is delivered as template forks, so integration is manual work, not a dependency swap.

eliteTeamPractices: Run odometry off the main loop at 100-250 Hz with a dedicated thread and a lock. 6328's templates ship PhoenixOdometryThread/SparkOdometryThread with a `static final Lock odometryLock` (ReentrantLock) and ODOMETRY_FREQUENCY = 250.0 on CANivore, 100.0 otherwise; CTRE's SwerveDrivetrain does the same natively. Measured effect: 50 Hz -> 250 Hz cuts odometry std dev from 0.180 m to 0.028 m (84%) while mean error only improves 23% — elite teams optimize for CONSISTENCY, not accuracy. https://docs.advantagekit.org/theory/high-frequency-odometry/

Pay for CANivore + Phoenix Pro timesync when running all-CTRE. With timesync, every device samples and publishes on the same tick with a device-side timestamp, giving best-possible latency compensation; CTRE measures ~15% mean and ~34% std-dev odometry improvement on top of frequency gains. https://v6.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/latest/docs/api-reference/mechanisms/swerve/swerve-overview.html

Apply the 254-derived swerve setpoint generator, not just wheel-speed desaturation. PathPlanner's SwerveSetpointGenerator limits module acceleration by motor torque, caps module torque at wheel-carpet friction to prevent slip, limits module rotation so centripetal force stays under friction (prevents sliding in curves), and models intra-module friction (lower max accel, higher max decel). https://pathplanner.dev/pplib-swerve-setpoint-generator.html

Characterize rather than guess — and characterize wheel radius, not just kS/kV. 6328 ships an in-code feedforward routine (2 s orient, 0.1 V/s ramp, least-squares fit) and a wheel-radius routine (spin in place at 0.05 rad/s^2 to 0.25 rad/s; radius = gyroDelta * driveBaseRadius / meanWheelDelta), explicitly recommending regular recharacterization to combat tread wear and carpet compression. Tuner X's generator does NOT characterize and its shipped gains are placeholders. https://docs.advantagekit.org/getting-started/template-projects/spark-swerve-template/

Set drive current limits from a measured slip test, not from a spec sheet. CTRE's documented procedure: put the robot against a wall on carpet, plot velocity and stator current in Tuner X, slowly increase voltage until velocity goes non-zero and stator current drops — that is the slip point (~130 A in their example), so limit below it (their swerve example: 120 A stator / 70 A supply per Kraken). https://v6.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/stable/docs/hardware-reference/talonfx/improving-performance-with-current-limits.html

Do skid detection and feed it into odometry trust. 1690 Orbit published the canonical FRC algorithm in their 2024 software sessions; 135's Consul framework ships it alongside momentum-based setpoint calculation. Elite teams use it to know when wheel odometry is lying and to lean harder on vision. https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/writeup-on-swerve-kinematics-and-basic-skid-detection/522622 and https://oa.pennrobotics.org/135-consul-frc-programming-framework/

Separate the three heading concepts explicitly. CTRE's API distinguishes seedFieldCentric() / seedFieldCentric(Rotation2d) (driver perspective), resetRotation(Rotation2d) (absolute blue-alliance-perspective heading), and setOperatorPerspectiveForward(Rotation2d) (called periodically, 0 deg on blue and 180 deg on red). Pose origin is ALWAYS blue; only the driver's forward flips. https://v6.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/latest/docs/api-reference/mechanisms/swerve/using-swerve-api.html

Use a ProfiledPIDController for heading lock rather than a plain P controller, with continuous input enabled. 6328's joystickDriveAtAngle uses KP=5.0, KD=0.4, max velocity 8.0 rad/s, max accel 20.0 rad/s^2, enableContinuousInput(-pi, pi). WPILib's HolonomicDriveController uses the same pattern: two PID controllers for x/y and one PROFILED controller for heading, because heading dynamics are decoupled from translation. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mechanical-Advantage/AdvantageKit/main/template_projects/sources/talonfx_swerve/src/main/java/frc/robot/commands/DriveCommands.java

Feed per-module wheel force feedforwards from the path planner into the drivetrain. Both PathPlanner (DriveFeedforwards) and Choreo emit them; CTRE's ApplyFieldSpeeds/ApplyRobotSpeeds accept them via withWheelForceFeedforwardsX/Y in newtons (WPILib convention, X forward). CTRE's own docs say its new-for-2026 WheelForceCalculator should be used only when your planner does NOT provide them. https://v6.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/latest/docs/api-reference/mechanisms/swerve/swerve-requests.html

Simulate with a real physics engine, not an ideal model. CTRE's swerve sim explicitly assumes no scrub and no wheel slip with constant drive inertia. Top teams use maple-sim (dyn4j rigid-body, collisions, game pieces, 2026 REBUILT field) so simulated autos transfer to the field. 135's Consul does the same with dyn4j directly, and tunes sim constants by matching simulated to real acceleration. https://shenzhen-robotics-alliance.github.io/maple-sim/swerve-simulation-overview/

Build for log replay from day one. AdvantageKit's IO layer + @AutoLog IOInputs makes logs the ground truth so a fix can be validated against a real match without re-running the robot; 135's Consul adopted the same three-layer split (IO = zero business logic, IOInputs = timestamped @AutoLog record, Subsystem = vendor-agnostic logic). Elite teams also swap PathPlanner's pathfinder for LocalADStarAK so pathfinding itself is deterministic under replay. https://docs.advantagekit.org/getting-started/template-projects/talonfx-swerve-template/

Tune steer with a very high kP and rely on feedback, not feedforward. Tuner X ships steer Slot0 kP=100, kD=0.5, kS=0.1, kV=1.91; 6328 notes that brushless motors make swerve turning exceptionally easy to control and that a well-tuned feedback-only controller gives nearly perfect tracking. https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-6328-mechanical-advantage-2026-build-thread/509595
pitfalls: WPILib 2026 SILENTLY changed SwerveModuleState optimization semantics. `optimize(Rotation2d)` and `cosineScale(Rotation2d)` are now void MUTATING INSTANCE methods; the static `SwerveModuleState optimize(SwerveModuleState, Rotation2d)` is deprecated. Code copied from 2023/2024 tutorials that does `state = SwerveModuleState.optimize(state, angle)` still compiles but is on a deprecated path, and code that half-migrates to `state.optimize(angle)` while still assigning the (void) return will not compile — teams then 'fix' it by deleting the call and lose optimization entirely, producing modules that take the long way around. https://github.wpilib.org/allwpilib/docs/release/java/edu/wpi/first/math/kinematics/SwerveModuleState.html

Forgetting ChassisSpeeds.discretize() causes the robot to arc sideways while translating and rotating simultaneously. It is never applied automatically by SwerveDriveKinematics. The mirror-image bug is DOUBLE discretization: PathPlanner's SwerveSetpointGenerator discretizes internally and its docs explicitly warn 'do not discretize speeds before or after using the setpoint generator.' https://pathplanner.dev/pplib-swerve-setpoint-generator.html

The alliance-flip trap. Pose origin is always blue; only the driver's 'forward' flips. Teams conflate 'zero the gyro' (operator perspective) with resetting the pose (absolute, blue-origin), which produces a robot that drives correctly in the shop and inverted on the red alliance, or an auto that starts from a mirrored pose. CTRE's three-method split (seedFieldCentric / resetRotation / setOperatorPerspectiveForward) exists precisely because of this. https://v6.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/latest/docs/api-reference/mechanisms/swerve/using-swerve-api.html

WPILib 2027 is a hard break and PumpkinLib's API surface must be designed for it NOW: `edu.wpi.first` -> `org.wpilib` and `frc::` -> `wpi::`; `ChassisSpeeds` renamed to `ChassisVelocities`; swerve and differential kinematics made IMMUTABLE; new `ChassisAccelerations` plus forward/inverse kinematics for accelerations; `RamseteCommand`, `SwerveControllerCommand` and `MecanumControllerCommand` REMOVED; Commands v3 introduced alongside v2 and `Command.schedule()` deprecated in v2; Java 25 / C++23; NetworkTables v3 removed; Shuffleboard, SmartDashboard, PathWeaver and RobotBuilder removed; roboRIO replaced by Systemcore (multiple CAN buses, Smart IO, onboard IMU); relays, analog outputs, SPI, ADIS16448/16470, ADXL345, ADXRS450, servos and Jaguar removed. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/latest/docs/yearly-overview/yearly-changelog.html

Phoenix 6 is breaking too. In the 2027 dev line (26.50.0-alpha-1) `SwerveRequest.ApplyFieldSpeeds`/`ApplyRobotSpeeds` are renamed `ApplyFieldVelocity`/`ApplyRobotVelocity` (tracking WPILib's ChassisSpeeds->ChassisVelocities rename), and `new <Device>(int id, String canbus)` constructors are already deprecated in 26.x and REMOVED in 2027 in favor of `new <Device>(int id, CANBus canbus)`. Any PumpkinLib code that names those request classes must be behind an adapter. https://api.ctr-electronics.com/phoenix6/latest/java/com/ctre/phoenix6/swerve/package-summary.html and https://v6.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/latest/docs/yearly-changes/yearly-changelog.html

Tuner X generates the project but does NOT characterize it. The shipped TunerConstants gains (drive kP=0.1, kS=0, kV=0.124; steer kP=100, kD=0.5, kS=0.1, kV=1.91) and slipCurrent=120 A are placeholders for a reference robot. Teams that never touch them get sluggish drive response and a slip current that is wrong for their weight and tread. https://v6.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/latest/docs/api-reference/mechanisms/swerve/swerve-builder-api.html

CTRE swerve simulation assumes no scrub, no wheel slip, and constant drive motor inertia — autos tuned only in CTRE sim will not transfer. It also models azimuth inertia and control lag, so modules lag their targets; CTRE recommends driving updateSimState from a 4 ms Notifier instead of the 20 ms robot loop to get realistic PID behavior. https://v6.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/latest/docs/api-reference/mechanisms/swerve/swerve-simulation.html

YAGSL's documented failure modes recur every season on Chief Delphi: robot freezing repeatedly while driving after a library update; module angles losing alignment under semi-aggressive driving with modules driving in reverse; turn motors spinning endlessly with no command (wrong steer inversion, or drive/steer CAN IDs swapped); odometry arcing during rotation when AprilTags are visible. YAGSL's own docs also tell all-CTRE teams to use Tuner X instead. https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/yagsl-swerve-modules-losing-alignment-when-driving/496307 and https://docs.yagsl.com/

Absolute encoder offsets and magnet mounting are the top hardware-adjacent software bug. If modules do not point straight on boot or after a straight command, offsets are wrong; a slightly-off offset drags a module and can draw penalties. Loose/unglued magnets drift the offset mid-competition. A library must ship a re-zeroing routine and a boot-time sanity check, not just a JSON field. https://docs.yagsl.com/configuring-yagsl/configuration/swerve-module-configuration

SwerveSetpointGenerator and PathPlanner's RobotConfig need massKG, MOI and wheelCOF. Nobody measures MOI; the entire community copies 74.088 kg / 6.883 kg*m^2 / 1.2 COF from the 6328 template. Wrong MOI makes slip limiting either useless (too permissive) or crippling (too conservative). https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mechanical-Advantage/AdvantageKit/main/template_projects/sources/spark_swerve/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/drive/DriveConstants.java

AdvantageKit templates are copy-and-own, not a dependency. There is no upgrade path — the 2026 templates contain 'many small changes and optimizations' versus 2025 that a team on last year's copy will never receive. A PumpkinLib that wraps the template inherits this; a PumpkinLib that adapts a team's existing Drive class does not. https://docs.advantagekit.org/whats-new/

Slew rate limiting is a traction band-aid, not a driver-feel feature. REV REMOVED the slew rate limiter from the MAXSwerve template because it is no longer needed with MAXSwerve 2.0 wheels. Shipping it on by default masks a tuning or traction problem and adds latency the driver feels. https://github.com/REVrobotics/MAXSwerve-Java-Template/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

Module order must be identical everywhere. SwerveDriveKinematics, SwerveDriveOdometry and PathPlanner's output all assume a consistent ordering (WPILib docs: 'it is important that the order in which you pass the SwerveModulePosition objects is the same as the order in which you created the kinematics object'; PathPlanner's swerve output is FL, FR, BL, BR). A library that accepts modules as an unordered map will produce subtly wrong kinematics. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/kinematics-and-odometry/swerve-drive-odometry.html

RamseteController is deprecated for removal (since 2025) — a rookie team following an old tank tutorial in 2026 is writing code that will not compile in 2027. LTVUnicycleController is the drop-in replacement, but note its guardrails: default tolerances x=0.0625 m, y=0.125 m, heading=2 rad, default maxVelocity 9 m/s, and it throws IllegalArgumentException if maxVelocity <=0 or >=15 m/s. https://github.wpilib.org/allwpilib/docs/release/java/edu/wpi/first/math/controller/LTVUnicycleController.html

Phoenix 6 26.1.0 changed a silent default: drive motor RotorToSensorRatio and SensorToMechanismRatio and steer motor SensorToMechanismRatio are now overridden to 1.0 so odometry and control behave as expected. Teams carrying over 2025 configs that set these themselves may see doubled/halved distances. https://api.ctr-electronics.com/changelog

YAGSL odometry runs at the 20 ms loop rate rather than on a high-frequency thread, and closed-loop PID on the controller is only available for SparkMAX and TalonFX. A team on YAGSL with mixed/PWM hardware is giving up the single biggest auto-consistency lever without being told. https://docs.yagsl.com/overview/our-features
